chapter.heading: The Shiloh Survey
chapter.v:
The land
had been subdued and lay before them. The Israelites gathered together at Shiloh and set up the Tent of Meeting.

However, seven
of the Israelite tribes had not received their land allocations.

So Joshua
asked the Israelites, “How long will you go on being reluctant to go and take possession of the land that the Lord gave your forefathers?

Choose three
men from each tribe and I will send them out to explore the land. Then they can write a description regarding the land allocations and bring it to me.

They are
to divide the land into seven parts, up to the boundary of Judah's land in the south and Joseph's land in the north.

Once you
have written the description about the land, divided into seven parts, you will bring it to me here and I will cast lots for you in the presence of the Lord our God.

But the
Levites do not receive a share, for their role as priests of the Lord is their allocation. Also, Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their allocation that Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave them on the east side of the Jordan.”

As the
men started out on their way to explore the land. Joshua told them, “Go throughout the land and write a description of what you find. Then return to me and I will cast lots for you in the presence of the Lord here in Shiloh.”

So the
men went and explored the land and wrote down on a scroll a description of the seven parts, recording the towns in each part. Then they returned to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh

where Joshua
cast lots for them in the presence of the Lord. There Joshua divided the land up and allotted the different parts to the remaining Israelite tribes.
chapter.heading: Benjamin
chapter.v:
The first
lot cast went to the tribe of Benjamin, by families. The land allotted lay between that of the tribe of Judah and the tribe of Joseph.

Their boundary
began at the Jordan, and went north of the slope of Jericho, west through the hill country, coming out at the wilderness of Beth-aven.

Then the
boundary went south to Luz (or Bethel) and on down to Ataroth-addar on the mountain south of Lower Beth-horon.

Here the
boundary turned south along the western side of the mountain facing Beth-horon, finishing at Kiriath-baal (or Kiriath-jearim), a town of the tribe of Judah. This was the western boundary.

The southern
boundary began at the edge of Kiriath-jearim. It ran to the spring at Nephtoah,

and then
down to the foot of the mountain that faces the valley of Ben-hinnom, at the north end of the valley of Rephaim. Then it went down the valley of Hinnom, along the slope near the Jebusite town, south towards En-rogel.

From there
it headed north to En-shemesh and on to Geliloth, opposite the heights of Adummim, and then on down to the Stone of Bohan (Reuben's son).

Then it
went along the ridge opposite the Jordan Valley to the north, and then down into the Jordan Valley itself.

From there
it ran along the north slope of Beth-hoglah, ending at the north bay of the Salt Sea, the southern end of the Jordan. This was the southern boundary.

The eastern
boundary was the Jordan.These were the boundaries around the land of the tribe of Benjamin, by families.

These were
the towns of the tribe of Benjamin, according to families: Jericho, Beth-hoglah, Emek-keziz,
Beth-arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel,
Avvim, Parah, Ophrah,

Kephar-ammoni, Ophni,
and Geba—twelve towns with their associated villages.

In addition:
Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,
Mizpah, Kephirah, Mozah,
Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,

Zela, Haeleph,
Jebus (or Jerusalem), Gibeah, and Kiriath-jearim—fourteen towns with their associated villages. This was the land allotted to the tribe of Benjamin, by families.
